rows.name: CLIFF_BYSTANDERS
rows.values: Integer, parsed with `atoi`. Text that is not a number counts as `0`. A value above the maximum is lowered to the maximum.
rows.default: Unset: the test uses the maximum.
rows.effect: Sets the number of bystander threads (extra waiting threads) that the test case `spin waiter storm at scale (56c cliff)` starts. A result below 8 threads makes the test case skip with the message `Not enough app cpus for a waiter storm`.
rows.notes: The maximum is 3 less than the number of application CPUs (CPU cores that the process pins its application threads to), and at most 53 threads. `0` and negative values also cause the skip.

rows.name: CMAKE_ARGV
rows.values: Path of a file that the fake `cmake` writes.
rows.default: Unset: the fake `cmake` stops with an unbound variable error.
rows.effect: The fake `cmake` writes its arguments, each ended by a NUL byte, to this file.
rows.notes: The test runs `make` with the fake `cmake` first on `PATH`. It then reads the file and checks the `-DTRON_INGEST_PLUGIN_BUNDLE` argument.

rows.name: COLLISION_STATE
rows.values: Path of a state file.
rows.default: Unset: the fake `mv` stops with a bash parameter error.
rows.effect: While this file is missing, the fake `mv` first creates the destination directory and records its path here.
rows.notes: The fake `mv` also writes an `owner` file into that directory. It then runs the real `mv` named by `REAL_MV`. The test runs `bin/ci/ci-shared-nfs.sh purge-entry` with it.

rows.name: DICE_PLAN_SENTINEL
rows.read_by: Python one-line program that the test generates (`bin/slice-tests/test_dice_lsf.py`)
rows.values: The test sets the text `expected`.
rows.default: Unset: the generated program fails with `KeyError`.
rows.effect: The test checks with this marker that `_slice_runtime_plan` of `bin/dice-lsf-runner` passes the given environment to the plan command.

rows.name: EXAMPLE_MOUNT
rows.values: Any text. The test sets an empty text, `ext4 /dev/example`, `nfs example-filer:/scratch` and `nfs4 example-filer:/scratch`.
rows.effect: The fake `findmnt` prints this text as its answer.
rows.notes: The test runs `bin/ci/ci-cleanup-build-artifacts.sh` with the fake `findmnt` first on `PATH`.

rows.name: EXAMPLE_MOUNT_STATUS
rows.values: Integer exit status, passed to `exit`. The test sets `0` and `1`.
rows.effect: The fake `findmnt` exits with this status.
rows.notes: The test runs `bin/ci/ci-cleanup-build-artifacts.sh` with the fake `findmnt` first on `PATH`.

rows.name: EXAMPLE_UNMOUNT
rows.values: Compared with the text `1`. The test sets `0` and `1`.
rows.effect: With the value `1`, the fake `findmnt` exits with status 1 when the file `storage-touched` exists.
rows.notes: The fake `ci-shared-nfs.sh` of the test creates the file `storage-touched`. The test expects `bin/ci/ci-cleanup-build-artifacts.sh` to fail in this case.

rows.name: FAKE_BRANCH
rows.values: Any text. The test sets `bot/slice-cost-data-genoa96`.
rows.default: Unset: the fake `gh` stops with an unbound variable error.
rows.effect: The fake `gh` prints this text as the head branch name in its answer to `gh pr view`.
rows.notes: The test runs `bin/ci/bench-refresh-ci.sh` with the fake program first on `PATH`.

rows.name: FAKE_CTEST_EXECUTABLE
rows.values: Path of an executable file.
rows.default: Unset: `gen/t_fixture` under the current directory of the fake `ctest`.
rows.effect: Sets the path of the test command that the fake `ctest` reports in its JSON output.

rows.name: FAKE_CTEST_LABELS
rows.values: JSON list of label strings, parsed with `json.loads`.
rows.default: Unset: `["fake"]`.
rows.effect: Sets the `LABELS` property that the fake `ctest` reports in its JSON output.

rows.name: FAKE_CTEST_WORKING_DIRECTORY
rows.values: Path of a directory.
rows.default: Unset: the current directory of the fake `ctest`.
rows.effect: Sets the `WORKING_DIRECTORY` property that the fake `ctest` reports in its JSON output.

rows.name: FAKE_CURRENT_BASE_SHA
rows.values: Any text. The test sets a commit id of 40 characters.
rows.default: Unset: the fake `git` stops with an unbound variable error.
rows.effect: The fake `git` prints this text as its answer to `git rev-parse`.
rows.notes: The test runs `bin/ci/bench-refresh-ci.sh` with the fake program first on `PATH`.

rows.name: FAKE_FLUSH_CHECK
rows.read_by: Fake `traced`, `traced_probes`, `perfetto` and `runtron` that the test generates (`perfetto/test_perfetto.py`)
rows.values: Any non-empty text turns it on. The test sets `1`.
rows.default: Unset: the fake programs write no line.
rows.effect: On `SIGINT` or `SIGTERM`, each fake program appends a line to the file `shutdown.order`.
rows.notes: The file is in the directory named by `FAKE_STATE`. The fake `perfetto` waits 0.2 seconds between its 2 lines. The fake `runtron` waits 0.2 seconds before its line. The tests check the lines and their order.

rows.name: FAKE_GH_ARGS
rows.values: Path of a file.
rows.default: Unset: the fake `gh` stops with an unbound variable error.
rows.effect: The fake `gh` appends its arguments as one line to this file.
rows.notes: The test runs `bin/ci/bench-refresh-ci.sh` with the fake program first on `PATH`.

rows.name: FAKE_GH_CLOSE_ARGS
rows.values: Path of a file.
rows.default: Unset: the fake `gh` stops with an unbound variable error.
rows.effect: The fake `gh` writes the arguments of `gh pr close` to this file.
rows.notes: The test runs `bin/ci/bench-refresh-ci.sh` with the fake program first on `PATH`.

rows.name: FAKE_GH_LIST_ARGS
rows.values: Path of a file.
rows.default: Unset: the fake `gh` stops with an unbound variable error.
rows.effect: The fake `gh` writes the arguments of `gh pr list` to this file.
rows.notes: The test runs `bin/ci/bench-refresh-ci.sh` with the fake program first on `PATH`.

rows.name: FAKE_ISSUE_BODY
rows.values: Path of a file.
rows.default: Unset: the fake `gh` stops with an unbound variable error.
rows.effect: The fake `gh` copies the file named by its last argument to this path.
rows.notes: The test runs `bin/ci/bench-refresh-ci.sh` with the fake program first on `PATH`.

rows.name: FAKE_MKDIR_RACE
rows.values: Any non-empty text turns it on. The test sets `1`.
rows.default: Unset: the fake `mkdir` creates the directory once.
rows.effect: The fake `mkdir` creates the requested directory under `instances/` twice. The second attempt fails.
rows.notes: The fake `mkdir` acts only on a directory directly under `$FAKE_TRACEFS/instances`. The test calls `prepare_tracefs` of `perfetto/launcher-common`.

evidence.quote: # instances/. FAKE_MKDIR_RACE lets another party create the instance first,
# so this mkdir fails. FAKE_MKDIR_TERM signals the launcher right after

rows.name: FAKE_MKDIR_READONLY
rows.values: Any non-empty text turns it on. The test sets `1`.
rows.default: Unset: both files stay writable.
rows.effect: After it creates the directory, the fake `mkdir` removes the write permission of `tracing_on` and `events/enable`.
rows.notes: The fake `mkdir` acts only on a directory directly under `$FAKE_TRACEFS/instances`. The test calls `prepare_tracefs` of `perfetto/launcher-common`.

rows.name: FAKE_MKDIR_TERM
rows.values: Any non-empty text turns it on. The test sets `1`.
rows.default: Unset: the fake `mkdir` sends no signal.
rows.effect: After it creates the directory, the fake `mkdir` sends `SIGTERM` to its parent process.
rows.notes: The fake `mkdir` acts only on a directory directly under `$FAKE_TRACEFS/instances`. The test calls `prepare_tracefs` of `perfetto/launcher-common`.

rows.name: FAKE_NIX_OUTPUT
rows.values: Path of a directory.
rows.effect: The fake `nix` links the `--out-link` path to this directory and prints this path.
rows.notes: The test runs `bin/dice-lsf-runner` with the fake `nix` first on `PATH`.

rows.name: FAKE_PERFETTO_EXIT
rows.values: Integer exit status, passed to `exit`. An empty text counts as unset. The test sets `0`, `23` and an empty text.
rows.default: Unset: after its readiness step, the fake `perfetto` runs until it gets `SIGINT` or `SIGTERM`.
rows.effect: After its readiness step, the fake `perfetto` waits and then exits with this status.
rows.notes: The readiness step writes one byte to the descriptor given by `--notify-fd`. Before the exit the program waits for the file named by `FAKE_PERFETTO_EXIT_MARKER`, or it sleeps `FAKE_PERFETTO_EXIT_DELAY` seconds. `FAKE_PERFETTO_EXIT_BEFORE_NOTIFY` and `FAKE_PERFETTO_NOTIFY_STATUS` make it exit earlier.

rows.name: FAKE_PERFETTO_EXIT_BEFORE_NOTIFY
rows.values: Any non-empty text turns it on. The test sets `1`.
rows.default: Unset: the fake `perfetto` does not exit at this point.
rows.effect: The fake `perfetto` exits before it writes the ready byte to the `--notify-fd` descriptor.
rows.notes: The exit status is the value of `FAKE_PERFETTO_EXIT`. The status is `0` when that variable is unset or empty.

rows.name: FAKE_PERFETTO_EXIT_DELAY
rows.values: Number of seconds, passed unchanged to `sleep`. The test sets `0.05` and `0.2`.
rows.default: Unset: 0 seconds.
rows.effect: The fake `perfetto` sleeps this many seconds before it exits with the status of `FAKE_PERFETTO_EXIT`.
rows.notes: It has an effect only when `FAKE_PERFETTO_EXIT` is not empty and `FAKE_PERFETTO_EXIT_MARKER` is unset or empty.

new_terms.definition: A CPU core in the list that a TRON process pins its application threads to.
An extra waiting thread that the test `t_mwaitx_cliff` starts next to the 2 threads that it measures.

notes: 23 of the 24 rows are fixtures (hand_set false). Only CLIFF_BYSTANDERS is set by a person. No row is dropped. 4 evidence quotes are an exact part of the source line and not the whole line: perfetto/test_perfetto.py:121, :124 and :125 (2 quotes). The rest of each line holds the shell operator made of 2 vertical bar characters, which the table format forbids.
